texts: A pacing lead found in the left ventricle should be removed surgically under direct vision, and a new lead placed in the right ventricle.
A lead in the left heart carries a high risk of thrombus and systemic embolism, including stroke.
After nine years the lead is encased in fibrous tissue and thrombus, and pulling it out through the veins risks tearing tissue and sending clot to the brain.
Under direct vision, the lead and any clot on it can be removed completely.
Leaving it in place, even with warfarin and aspirin, keeps the embolic risk for life in a 25-year-old.
In the picture, Franky opens the red room and pulls the stray wire out by hand under a bright lantern, and a new wire goes to the blue room.
Memory hook: a wire in the red room comes out by hand, in the light.
